about.author: Zyphullen

automatic_checks.what: Structural checks run by a script on every build (src/audit.py, report in AUDIT-v0.7.md): every card has a colour and at least one source, links point at cards that exist, share links are exact, the data hash is the same in every file, counts match, and every source URL was fetched to see that it answers.
automatic_checks.not: They do not read the science. Passing them does not mean a claim is right, only that it is labelled, sourced and linked.

science_review.what: A science review means a person with the right expertise reads each claim against its sources and decides whether it is right, up to date and fairly coloured.
science_review.how_to_help: Every card has a Suggest a fix button (e-mail). Please check claims against the listed sources and say what looks wrong.

about.certainty_rule: green = established (known science, or a defined / proved result in Maths); orange = leading idea / partial progress; red = unknown / open problem. A link takes the colour of its less-certain end.

suggest_a_fix.subject: Echo Atlas fix: <Card name> (<card id>)
suggest_a_fix.note: Every card has a Suggest a fix button that opens a prefilled e-mail (section, card, card id, version, page link). Card ids: fntu/<id>, maths/<id>, history/<id>-<n>, cell/<id>, body/<id>, planet/<id>, element/<symbol>, <section>/link/<from>><to>.

about.what_this_is: Index of the Echo Atlas AI data files. Load only the section you need.

files.about: Universe → Us map and ring (on the site, Explore → From Nothing to Us → Map / Ring / History): from "Before the Big Bang?" to us, including Chain Theory (one candidate starting point, orange) and its open gap (red).

A dated timeline of the universe from the Big Bang to today: the first second, the first nuclei and light, cosmic dawn, galaxies and the Sun, Earth and life. The time scale changes between eras. On the site it is also the History view of From Nothing to Us (Explore → From Nothing to Us → History).

A zoomable 3D tour through real NASA / ESA / Hubble / Webb / Planck / Gaia images, one stop per scale: Earth, the Sun, our sky (the Milky Way from inside), a spiral galaxy like ours (M101), Webb's First Deep Field and the cosmic microwave background. Each stop has its real size, the image credit and licence, sources and links to other sections.

Forces, particles and light: the four fundamental interactions, the Standard Model, antimatter, dark matter, light, relativity and quantum electrodynamics, with the open questions (quantum gravity, unification, neutrino mass, baryon asymmetry).

Cells, evolution and life systems: the molecules of life, DNA and the genetic code, cells, the origin and evolution of life, photosynthesis, respiration, ecosystems and bodies, with the open questions (origin of life, life beyond Earth, consciousness). The Virtual Cell and Human Body explorers sit with Biology on the site; their cards are in virtual-cell.json and human-body.json.
Maths map and ring: definitions, proved theorems, partial progress and open problems across 16 branches.
A dated timeline (one or more landmarks for every Maths node), across five eras. Proposed ideas are kept apart from proofs.

Every red (unknown) and orange (we think) card already in the other sections, in one list, with how many rival ideas and tests each has. No new science: the full card is in its own section file (open it with share_url).
Earth from space to the inner core: atmosphere layers, ocean, crust, mantle and core, with real depths in km.
A typical human cell: organelles, molecules, atoms and living processes, drawn to scale where possible.
Organs, bones, muscles, vessels and nerves, and which kinds of cell build each part.

All 118 elements with symbols, groups and simplified cosmic origins (where each element was mostly made). The Atom Sandbox uses this table; it is a teaching toy with preset reactions, not a quantum simulator.
